realEstate.title: Real Estate Platform
realEstate.description: A modern real estate platform offering property listings, smart filtering, and user-friendly design.
realEstate.overview: This SaaS platform is designed for real estate agencies and individual property owners. It allows users to browse, search, and filter properties by location, type, and price. caros.title: Caros — Multi-Tenant Dealership & Rental SaaS
caros.description: A bilingual white-label platform for showrooms and rental agencies — four surfaces from one deployment, with double-booking prevented by a database constraint.
caros.overview: Caros gives a showroom or rental agency its own branded, bilingual site with the inventory, lead and booking tooling behind it. One dealer is one row, resolved at runtime from the request host, so onboarding needs no deploy. A single codebase serves four distinct surfaces — dealer storefront, dealer dashboard, platform operator console and the marketing site — each with its own document and its own colour system.
features: Four surfaces from one codebase — dealer storefront, dealer dashboard, platform operator console and marketing site — each resolving its tenant differently: by request host, by signed-in user, or by no tenant at all.
A car cannot be double-booked. A Postgres EXCLUDE constraint refuses two overlapping confirmed bookings, so the engine rejects the write rather than application code that can be bypassed.

A vehicle carries three independent axes — listing lifecycle, storefront visibility, and whether the physical car may leave the lot — kept separate on purpose, because conflating them is what silently mis-sells a car.
Tenant isolation by tenant_id plus Row-Level Security, proven by an automated test that signs in as a real second tenant and asserts denial.
An append-only vehicle history written by database triggers, with no update or delete policy on the table at all — the only property that makes a history worth reading.
Every vehicle gets an indexable page with JSON-LD, printable QR codes that survive slug changes, and a Web Push notification to the dealer the moment a lead arrives.
caros.audience: Car showrooms and rental agencies replacing an agency-built site or a paper diary.
caros.goal: Put a dealer live on their own brand without a project — and make concurrent rental bookings provably safe.
caros.purpose: Sole engineer across four surfaces: architecture, Postgres schema and constraints, dashboards, storefront and design system.

sello.title: Sello — Multi-Tenant Social-Commerce Platform
sello.description: A multi-tenant commerce OS: one codebase and one deployment serve many isolated merchants, each on its own subdomain with its own brand, catalogue and dashboard.
sello.overview: Sello turns a social-media merchant into a real storefront. One deployment serves many fully isolated tenants, and three independent axes decide what a store is: the vertical decides what the data is, the archetype decides how it looks, and the brand decides its colours. Above them sits a platform operator console. I built it end to end — schema and RLS, server-side order pricing, the section engine, the dashboard and the storefront.
features: Tenant resolved at runtime from the request host and isolated by Postgres Row-Level Security — not by routing or application code. An automated test signs in as a second tenant and asserts denial.
Orders are priced only by the server. One SECURITY DEFINER RPC re-prices products and delivery from the database, so the client sends ids and quantities and can never send a price.

The dashboard adapts to the kind of store. A vertical — clothing, food, beauty or general — decides which product fields exist and their Arabic vocabulary. Attributes live in a JSON bag, so changing a store vertical never deletes what was already entered.
No component may branch on the vertical. Forms read a field list and render what they find, which keeps adding a fifth store type a typed code change rather than a sweep through the UI.

The tenant row is the page. A JSON-driven section engine — 10 types, 17 schema-validated variants, four design archetypes — lets a merchant compose and theme their storefront behind a draft/publish model.

Five route groups from one deployment, including a platform operator console bound to the root domain: a merchant host asking for /admin gets a 404, not a 403, and every platform write lands in an append-only audit log.
Arabic-first RTL throughout, with lint, typecheck and a custom design-system gate enforced in CI.
sello.audience: Social-media merchants who need a real storefront, and the operator team running the platform behind them.
sello.goal: One codebase, many isolated merchants — with pricing that cannot be tampered with from the browser.
sello.purpose: Sole engineer: architecture, Postgres schema and RLS, order pricing, the section engine, dashboard, storefront and design system.

xBus.title: X-Bus — Intercity Bus Booking Marketplace
xBus.description: A bus booking marketplace where seat selection holds up under concurrency — per-seat locks with server-issued TTLs, idempotent booking, and a test suite that proves it.
xBus.overview: X-Bus is an intercity bus booking marketplace: passengers search trips, pick seats on a live seat map and book, while operators publish trips and check passengers in. Every piece of critical logic lives in Postgres rather than the client, behind one response envelope with a closed set of error codes — and the concurrency guarantees are proven by tests against a real database, not asserted.
features: Per-seat locking under a server-issued TTL, so two passengers can never hold the same seat — verified by a concurrency suite that races real clients against a real database.
Idempotent booking creation that survives double-submits and expired locks, keeping the passenger in the flow instead of failing them at the last step.
All critical logic lives in Postgres RPCs, never in the client. Every response shares one envelope with a closed set of error codes the UI branches on — never on an HTTP status.
A real-database test suite with no mocks — concurrency, RLS, security, booking and operator flows — plus k6 load scripts aimed directly at seat locking and the seat map.
Mock fixtures are opt-in, never opt-out. An unset variable lands on real data, and a production build with mocks enabled throws at load rather than quietly serving fake answers to real users.
Arabic-first RTL and mobile-first, with the database client typed from the schema so a renamed RPC argument fails at compile time instead of at runtime.
xBus.audience: Passengers booking intercity trips, and the operators publishing them and checking passengers in.
xBus.goal: Make seat selection provably correct under concurrency — and prove it with tests rather than assert it.
xBus.purpose: Sole engineer: Postgres RPCs and migrations, the client/server contract, the booking interface, and the test and load-testing setup.
